title: Natural Language Processing
overview: NLP is AI understanding, processing, and generating human language.

blocks.title: What is What is NLP & Tokenization?
blocks.body: NLP is AI understanding, processing, and generating human language.
bullets: NLP = Natural Language Processing — AI working with human language
Why language is hard for AI — same word can mean very different things depending on context
Tokenization — splitting text into individual words or parts AI can process
Bag of Words — representing text by counting how often each word appears
This concept is fundamental to AI development.

analogy.title: Think of Tokenization as Slicing a Pizza
analogy.description: Split text into smaller pieces for processing

code.code:
text = "hello world ai"
tokens = text.split()
print(tokens)

blocks.title: Tokenizing Text & Bag of Words
blocks.instructions: Tokenize a sentence and count word frequencies (Bag of Words).
blocks.starterCode:
text = "the cat sat on the mat"
tokens = text.split()
print(f"Tokens: {tokens}")
from collections import Counter
bow = Counter(tokens)
for word, count in bow.items():
    print(f"  '{word}': {count}")

blocks.title: What is Word Embeddings & Large Language Models?
blocks.body: Word embeddings represent words as numbers. LLMs are very large neural networks trained on massive text.
bullets: Word Embeddings — words represented as numbers so AI can find similarities
Word math: King - Man + Woman = Queen — AI can do this kind of reasoning
Language Models predict the next word given the previous words
LLMs (Large Language Models) — trained on massive text data (GPT, Gemini, Claude)
Transformers — the architecture behind modern LLMs — processes all words at once

analogy.title: Think of Word Embeddings as a Map of Meanings
analogy.description: Similar words are close together in vector space

code.code:
# Word embedding: cosine similarity
vecs = {"king": [0.8, 0.6], "queen": [0.7, 0.5], "apple": [0.2, 0.9]}
k, q = vecs["king"], vecs["queen"]
sim = sum(a*b for a,b in zip(k,q)) / (sum(a*a for a in k)**0.5 * sum(b*b for b in q)**0.5)
print(f"king ↔ queen similarity: {sim:.2f}")

blocks.title: Computing Word Similarity
blocks.instructions: Calculate similarity between word pairs using letter overlap (simplified embedding).
blocks.starterCode:
# Word similarity using character overlap
def similarity(word1, word2):
    common = len(set(word1) & set(word2))
    total = len(set(word1) | set(word2))
    return common / total if total > 0 else 0
pairs = [("king", "queen"), ("king", "apple"), ("apple", "orange")]
for w1, w2 in pairs:
    sim = similarity(w1, w2)
    print(f"{w1} ↔ {w2}: {sim:.2f}")
blocks.solution:
def similarity(word1, word2):
    common = len(set(word1) & set(word2))
    total = len(set(word1) | set(word2))
    return common / total if total > 0 else 0
pairs = [("king", "queen"), ("king", "apple"), ("apple", "orange")]
for w1, w2 in pairs:
    sim = similarity(w1, w2)
    print(f"{w1} ↔ {w2}: {sim:.2f}")
blocks.hint: Word embeddings place similar words close together in vector space. Similar words share more common letters.

blocks.title: What is NLP Steps?
blocks.body: How text is processed by LLMs.
bullets: Step 1: Take raw text input from user
Step 2: Tokenize — split into words or subwords
Step 3: Convert tokens to numbers (word embeddings)
Step 5: Model predicts next token → generates output text

analogy.title: Think of an LLM as a Very Well-Read Librarian
analogy.description: Predicts the next word based on billions of examples

blocks.title: Text Tokenization & Bag of Words
blocks.code:
# Basic NLP: tokenization and word frequency
text = "the cat sat on the mat"

# Tokenize: split into words
tokens = text.lower().split()
print(f"Tokens: {tokens}")

# Bag of words: count frequency
word_counts = {}
for word in tokens:
    word_counts[word] = word_counts.get(word, 0) + 1

for word, count in sorted(word_counts.items()):
    print(f"  '{word}': {count}")

blocks.title: Practice Exercise
blocks.instructions: Ask ChatGPT the same question 3 different ways — write down how the answer changes each time
blocks.hint: See how minor wording changes affect the output.

keyTakeaways.text: NLP lets AI understand and generate human language
Tokenization splits text into pieces AI can process
Bag of Words counts word frequency to represent text
Word embeddings place words in number space — similar words are close together
LLMs are trained on massive text and predict the next word
Transformers process all words at once — powering GPT, Gemini, Claude

whatYouLearned: What NLP is and how it processes language
